candidate.title: G&T-seq
candidate.scope: The middle G&T-seq row of the assigned Illumina poster crop, matched to the page-118 G&T-Seq heading and figure caption: single-cell lysis, bead capture and RNA/DNA separation, on-bead Smart-seq2 transcriptome processing and separate MDA genome amplification, branch-specific sequencing, then paired RNA/genome alignment. Full-image inventory also identifies a separate scM&T-seq row above (scBS-seq DNA branch), a separate partially cropped scTrio-seq row below (supernatant/nucleus routes), and clipped neighboring SCRB-Seq text at the top edge. These are neighboring method entries, not alternatives within the captioned G&T-seq schematic. Smart-seq2 and MDA are named components, not additional target assays. This is a schematic architecture, not a complete execution protocol.

operations.label: Streptavidin magnetic bead with mRNA capture primer

method_scopes.rationale: All nine local operations belong to the explicitly labeled middle G&T-seq row, independently reproduced and captioned on catalogue page 118. Capture and separation are distinct boundaries; upper and lower Sequence instances act on different materials under one shared caption. The final Align RNA and genome endpoint integrates data from both branches. The left single-cell/RNA/DNA drawing identifies biological targets and is not an additional molecular splitting operation. Neighboring assay rows do not expand the card target. The original Macaulay publication is verified from its identity and abstract; the detailed depicted chemistry rests on image and catalogue evidence. Angermueller full text corroborates the explicitly G&T-seq-derived separation/RNA interface while describing a different DNA adaptation.
